m0.title: Welcome to Lorenmar
m0.text: A messenger found you on the road: Commander Varric wants to see you the moment you arrive. He waits in the town square.
m0.fin: So you are the one the messenger found. Good. Aldara needs blades, and it needs them now.

m1.title: A Call to Arms
m1.text: Goblins, orcs and worse are pouring out of the wilds, and every region has a guardian of its own. Scout Maren holds our outpost in the Green Fields. Go to her, and do as she says.
m1.fin: Varric sent you? Then you are just in time. I have three scouts and a hundred problems.

m2.title: Wings in the Dark
m2.text: Bat swarms roost in the caves and hunt at every hour now. They have already blinded one of my scouts. Thin them out.
m2.fin: Quieter already. Thank you. Now for the real trouble.

m3.title: Goblin Scouting
m3.text: The goblins have made a camp and they are digging in. Find it, see what they are up to, and make them regret it.
m3.fin: Tents, fires and too many knives. They are building an army, and someone is leading them.

m4.title: Moonpetal Remedy
m4.text: Goblin blades are dirty and my scouts are sick with it. Moonpetal grows wild in the meadows; it glows pale blue. Bring me five blossoms.
m4.fin: That will do nicely. Take some of the tonic for yourself.

m5.title: Trophy Ears
m5.text: Varric pays for proof, not stories. The goblins wear their clan marks on their ears. Bring me six.
m5.fin: Every one of these carries the same mark: the Warchief's. Now we know who we are fighting.

m6.title: Topple the Warchief
m6.text: The Goblin Warchief holds a ring of stones east of here and every goblin in the Fields answers to him. Cut off the head and the body will scatter. Choose something from our stores for the fight.
m6.fin: The Warchief is dead! The Fields will breathe easier tonight. Take your pick of the spoils.

m7.title: The Highland Road
m7.text: The goblins were only the start. Something stirs the dead in the Ashen Highlands. Ranger Dask keeps watch there. Go north to him.
m7.fin: Maren's runner? No, you have the look of a fighter. Good. I need one.

m8.title: Orc Raiders
m8.text: Orc warbands raid the highland road every night. Break them before they reach the farms.
m8.fin: That will make them think twice. Orcs respect a bloody nose.

m9.title: Stolen Warbanners
m9.text: The orcs fly banners stolen from our own villages. Find their palisade and take them back. Every banner they lose is a war they cannot call.
m9.fin: Our colours, back where they belong. The villagers will not forget this.

m10.title: The Restless Dead
m10.text: The old graveyards have emptied. Skeleton lords walk the ridges with their swords still sharp. Put them back in the ground.
m10.fin: Dust to dust. But something called them up, and it is still out there.

m11.title: Grave Relics
m11.text: The dead are bound by relics buried with them: old amulets and carved bones. Dig them up from the barrows so they cannot be used again.
m11.fin: Cold to the touch, every one. Father Aldous will want to see these.

m12.title: Break the Tyrant
m12.text: The Bone Tyrant, a warlord dead for three hundred years, sits on a throne of skulls and calls his soldiers from the earth. End him.
m12.fin: The Tyrant is dust! You have done what our whole garrison could not.

m13.title: Into the Mire
m13.text: The Tyrant was not the source. The dark comes from the Shadowfen to the south. Warden Ilse knows the bog better than anyone alive.
m13.fin: Dask sends me a hero now? The bog must be worse than I thought.

m14.title: Knights of Shadow
m14.text: Knights in black armour ride through the fen. They were ours once, sworn to Lorenmar, until the shadow took them. Free them.
m14.fin: Whatever holds them is stronger than an oath. I have seen it in their eyes.

m15.title: Shadow Sigils
m15.text: Each fallen knight carries a sigil burned into steel. Bring them to me; I will learn who forged them.
m15.fin: Dragon script. Something great and old is behind this.

m16.title: Bogbloom Antidote
m16.text: Wyrm venom is killing my wardens. Bogbloom, the green flower that glows at the water's edge, draws it out. I need six.
m16.fin: You may have saved half my company. Take some of the antidote with you.

m17.title: Wyrm Hunt
m17.text: Blood wyrms nest in the deep pools, and they grow bolder every night. They are the dragon's spawn. Cull them.
m17.fin: With the wyrms gone, the dragon will have to come out itself.

m18.title: Slay the Dragon
m18.text: The Shadowfen Dragon. It turned my knights and it breeds the wyrms. Its lair lies deep in the fen. Kill it, and the bog is ours again.
m18.fin: The dragon is dead! I never thought I would live to say those words. Take what you like from its hoard.

m19.title: Into the Warrens
m19.text: The goblins that survived the Warchief fled underground to a Goblin King who hoards weapons for a new war. Clear the Goblin Warrens (Dungeons, J).
m19.fin: The Goblin King fallen and his hoard broken up. The Fields are safe for a generation.

m20.title: The Frozen North
m20.text: The dragon's sigils were forged in the north. Huntsman Brom holds the Frostpeak outpost. Dress warmly.
m20.fin: Ilse sent you? Then you are either very brave or very foolish. Both help out here.

m21.title: Troll Country
m21.text: Frost trolls have come down from the peaks and they are eating my hounds. Drive them back.
m21.fin: Big, stupid and tough to kill. You made it look easy.

m22.title: Troll Tusks
m22.text: Troll tusk makes the best arrowheads there is. Bring me eight and we will be ready for whatever comes down that mountain.
m22.fin: Fine ivory. My hunters will sleep better.

m23.title: Frost Lilies
m23.text: Frost lilies grow where the snow never melts. Brewed down, they keep a body warm through the night. My people need them.
m23.fin: That will keep us through the storm. Take a flask for the road.

m24.title: Wraiths and Harpies
m24.text: Ice wraiths drift over the tundra and harpies nest on the crags above. Both answer to the Giant King. Clear the way to his throne.
m24.fin: The way is open. Now only the King stands in our way.

m25.title: The Giant King
m25.text: The Frost Giant King forged those dragon sigils in ice and shadow. His hall stands among the peaks. Go and topple him.
m25.fin: The King has fallen! The songs will be about you now. Take your share of his treasure.

m26.title: Crypt of Bones
m26.text: The lich Morvain raised the Tyrant and taught the King his dark craft. He hides in the Crypt of Bones (Dungeons, J). Finish him.
m26.fin: Morvain is gone. The dead will stay dead.

m27.title: Ashes and Embers
m27.text: Morvain's notes speak of a fire lord in the Emberwaste who feeds the whole darkness. Ashwalker Kael guides travellers there.
m27.fin: You came across the ash on foot? Then you might last a day. Let us make it two.

m28.title: Imps of the Waste
m28.text: Fire imps swarm the dunes, setting traps and burning caravans. Stamp them out.
m28.fin: Fewer imps, fewer fires. Simple arithmetic.

m29.title: Cinder Cores
m29.text: Magma golems walk on molten hearts called cinder cores. Break the golems, bring me their hearts, and we can light the beacon towers again.
m29.fin: Still warm. The beacons will burn for years.

m30.title: Ember Ore
m30.text: Ember ore glows orange in the rock. Blades forged with it do not melt in the Infernal Lord's fire. Gather six chunks.
m30.fin: Good ore. Thorin in Lorenmar will pay double for any you find later.

m31.title: Salamander Skins
m31.text: Ash salamanders guard the approach to the Infernal Lord. Their hides turn flame; kill them, and we will have fireproof cloaks.
m31.fin: The path to the Lord is clear. May the ash not have you.

m32.title: Dethrone the Inferno
m32.text: The Infernal Lord sits on a throne of living fire. Kill him and the Emberwaste will finally cool.
m32.fin: The fires are dying down. For the first time in memory, it rained ash-free today.

m33.title: The Frozen Depths
m33.text: Queen Glacia, the Giant King's sister, has sealed herself in the Frozen Depths (Dungeons, J). While she lives, the north will not rest.
m33.fin: The Ice Queen is gone. Frostpeak owes you everything.

m34.title: Edge of the World
m34.text: With the Lord dead, we can see what he was guarding: a tear in the world to the east. Seer Vhal watches the Void Reach.
m34.fin: There you are. Exactly on time, as foreseen.

m35.title: Stalkers in the Dark
m35.text: Void stalkers slip between the shadows and hunt anything that glows. They will find you. Be ready.
m35.fin: You came back. I saw that you would, but it is still a relief.

m36.title: Void Shards
m36.text: Shards of the Void crystallise where reality is thinnest. With six I can map the tear and find the one who opened it.
m36.fin: The pattern is clear now. The Void has an Emperor, and he is waiting for you.

m37.title: Horrors and Star Eaters
m37.text: Abyssal horrors crawl from the tear, and star eaters drink the light above them. Both must be driven back.
m37.fin: The tear flickers. It is weakening.

m38.title: Stardust
m38.text: Star eaters hold stolen starlight inside them. Bring it back and I will weave it into a ward against the Emperor's mind.
m38.fin: The ward is woven. His voice will not reach you now.

m39.title: The Molten Forge
m39.text: Ignar the Forgemaster makes the Emperor's weapons in the Molten Forge (Dungeons, J). Shut his forge down.
m39.fin: No more blades for the Void. Only the Emperor himself remains.

m40.title: End of the Void
m40.text: The Void Emperor waits at the heart of the Reach. I have seen many endings to this fight. Make it the good one.
m40.fin: The good ending. I knew it. Mostly.

m41.title: The Shining Lands
m41.text: One last vision: a fallen angel in the Elysian Expanse. Everything that happened began with her. Lady Seraphine leads the crusade there.
m41.fin: The Seer's champion. The Light has sent us an answer.

m42.title: Songs of the Deep
m42.text: Naga sirens sing our soldiers into the lagoons and they never come back. Silence them, and bring back their pearls; the songs live in them.
m42.fin: The lagoons are quiet. Only the waves now.

m43.title: The Thundering Herd
m43.text: Centaur warlords ride against the crusade day and night. Break their charge.
m43.fin: Their herd is scattered. Now for the ones in the sky.

m44.title: Wings of Ruin
m44.text: Fallen seraphs. They were the Archon's guard, and they fell with her. Grant them rest, and bring back their halos.
m44.fin: Tarnished, but not beyond cleansing. Father Aldous will know what to do.

m45.title: Living Heartwood
m45.text: The elder treants have turned against us, maddened by the Archon. Their living heartwood can still be saved. Gather it, and fell the ones too far gone.
m45.fin: The grove will grow again. You have my thanks.

m46.title: The Void Sanctum
m46.text: The Hollow King guards the last door between the Void and the world: the Void Sanctum (Dungeons, J). Close it forever.
m46.fin: The door is closed. Only the Archon remains.

m47.title: Fall of the Archon
m47.text: The Seraphim Archon. She opened the Void so she could be worshipped as a god. End her reign, champion.
m47.fin: It is over. The Light shines on Aldara again, and it shines on you.

m48.title: Champion of Aldara
m48.text: Go home, champion. Commander Varric will want to hear it from you.
m48.fin: I sent a stranger to the Green Fields and a legend came back. Aldara is yours to protect now. Welcome home.

s1.title: Herbs for the Stew
s1.text: My famous stew needs moonpetal, and the goblins have scared off my usual forager. Six blossoms from the Green Fields and the first bowl is yours.
s1.fin: Smell that! Here, your payment, and a flask of something stronger than stew.

s2.title: Pest Control
s2.text: Anything with teeth in the Green Fields is fair game. Fifteen of them, and my scouts can sleep.
s2.fin: The Fields are safer. Thank you.

s3.title: Rest for the Restless
s3.text: Word reaches me of the dead rising in the Highlands. Those were good people once. Give them back their rest.
s3.fin: May they sleep in peace this time. Bless you.

s4.title: Relics of the Faith
s4.text: The barrows hold old relics of our faith, stolen long ago. Bring them home to the cathedral where they belong.
s4.fin: These have not seen candlelight in three centuries. Thank you, child.

s5.title: Highland Sweep
s5.text: Clear the ridges of anything hostile. Twenty kills anywhere in the Ashen Highlands.
s5.fin: The ridges are quiet. Good work.

s6.title: Purge the Bog
s6.text: The bog breeds monsters faster than we can count them. Thin every kind you find.
s6.fin: The wardens can patrol again. You have our thanks.

s7.title: Wyrmscale Harvest
s7.text: Blood wyrm scale takes an edge better than any steel. Bring me eight and I will make it worth your while.
s7.fin: Beautiful. Here, pick something from my rack.

s8.title: Troll Hide Leather
s8.text: Frost troll hide makes armour that shrugs off a sword. Six hides, if you can stand the smell.
s8.fin: Phew. But it will make fine leather. Here is your coin.

s9.title: Frostfire Ale
s9.text: Frostfire Ale needs frost lilies from the northern peaks. It is the drink every adventurer asks for and I have run dry.
s9.fin: The first barrel is yours. Well, one flask of it.

s10.title: Frozen Plumes
s10.text: Harpy plumes fletch arrows that never miss in the wind. Eight will do.
s10.fin: Good feathers. The hunters thank you.

s11.title: The Frozen Frontier
s11.text: Anything that hunts on the tundra hunts us. Thirty of them, and the frontier holds.
s11.fin: The frontier holds. Thanks to you.

s12.title: Ore for the Forge
s12.text: Kael says there is ember ore in the Waste. I have not held a chunk in twenty years. Bring me six and I will forge you something special.
s12.fin: Ha! Twenty years! Choose what I make you.

s13.title: Imp Horns
s13.text: Ground imp horn keeps the ash out of wounds. Ten horns.
s13.fin: That will heal a lot of burns.

s14.title: Scorched Earth
s14.text: The Waste teems with fire-born beasts. Thirty of them, and the caravans can move again.
s14.fin: The caravans are rolling. Well fought.

s15.title: Light Against the Dark
s15.text: I have prayed on the reports from the Void Reach. Those horrors are an affront to the Light. Burn them away.
s15.fin: The Light is with you. I have always known it.

s16.title: Starmetal
s16.text: Void shards melted with steel make starmetal. No one has made it in a thousand years. Let us be the first.

s17.title: Edge of Reality
s17.text: Every creature of the Void you slay keeps the tear from widening. Thirty-five of them.
s17.fin: The tear holds. As I foresaw.

s18.title: Elysian Crusade
s18.text: The crusade needs a champion at the front. Forty enemies of the Expanse, any kind.
s18.fin: The crusade marches on because of you.

s19.title: Centaur Warhorns
s19.text: Without their warhorns the centaurs cannot rally. Take them.
s19.fin: Silence on the plains. Well done.

s20.title: Blessing of Heartwood
s20.text: A cathedral altar of living heartwood would be a blessing for a thousand years. Would you bring some back from the Expanse?
s20.fin: It is still warm, still alive. A miracle. Bless you.

k1.title: The Road to Valcrest
k1.text: A royal courier died at my outpost last night. His letter bore the King's seal: the Crown calls every blade that can reach Valcrest. Valcrest lies at the far south-eastern end of the island. Two roads lead there: east through the Brigand Marches, or south through the Gloomwood. Few make it. Captain Roderic Vale keeps the Sunset Gate. Go.
k1.fin: You came through the Marches on your own feet? Then the courier did not die for nothing. Welcome to Valcrest.

k2.title: The Red Hand
k2.text: Every Red Hand cutthroat wears the insignia on his cloak. Bring me eight of them and I will know how many we are really fighting. Bring me more and the Watch will buy you a drink.
k2.fin: Eight hands. Somewhere out there, eight cloaks are cold. Good.

k3.title: Crossbows on the Kingsroad
k3.text: The crossbowmen sit in the rocks above the road and shoot the drivers first. Clear them out and the caravans can move again.
k3.fin: The Harvest caravan made it in this morning. They asked who cleared the road. I told them.

k4.title: The King of Thieves
k4.text: Red Jack holds a fortified camp in the southern Marches and wears a crown he stole from a royal caravan. Cut off the head of the Red Hand. Bring back the crown if you can. Choose something from the Watch armoury for the fight.
k4.fin: The King of Thieves is dead? Then the Marches will belong to the road again, in time. Take your pick, and my thanks.

k5.title: Rats in the Undercity
k5.text: Something is driving the rats up out of the sewers. Go down through any of the grates in the Commons, thin them out, and find whatever is giving them orders. Then come back up. Please come back up.
k5.fin: The Rat King? Light preserve us. The sewermen will be drinking your health for a month.

k6.title: Moonsilver Dew
k6.text: In the Gloomwood the dew still gathers silver on the flowers that remember the old forest. The Moonwell is growing dim. Bring me six drops of moonsilver dew and I will sing it bright again.
k6.fin: Listen: the water is singing. You have done Silverbough a kindness it will remember for a very long time.

k7.title: The Hexwood Coven
k7.text: The Hexwood witches are poisoning the Gloomwood root and branch. Every one of them you stop gives the forest a year to heal.
k7.fin: The birds are singing at the forest edge again. Only a few. It is a beginning.

k8.title: Scales for the Forge
k8.text: Wyvern scale, quenched in the Great Forge, makes the finest shield-facing there is. The wyverns nest in the Gloomwood oaks. Bring me six scales, and try to bring back all your fingers.
k8.fin: Ha! Look at the grain on these. The Royal Knights will be fighting over the shields.

k9.title: Troll Hide Bellows
k9.text: The great bellows are cracking and ox-hide burns through in a week. Troll hide does not burn. Five hides from the Gloomwood trolls, if you please.
k9.fin: These will breathe for the Forge for a hundred years. You have a dwarf's gratitude, which is heavier than it looks.

k10.title: The Wyrm of the Wood

obj.t: Gloomfang, the Wyrm of the Wood

k10.text: The wyverns answer to a mother wyrm the elves call Gloomfang, older than the blight and twice as bitter. Kill her and the Gloomwood can begin to heal. Take a weapon from my own racks for it.
k10.fin: Gloomfang is dead. I would not have believed it from anyone else. Choose, and tell the tale in every tavern in the city.

k11.title: An Audience with the King
k11.text: His Majesty will receive you in the throne room. Enter by the great doors behind me, walk the length of the hall, bow when you reach the dais and do not touch anything that is gold. Which is most things.
k11.fin: His Majesty was pleased with you. That is rarer than you might think.

k12.title: Oathbreakers
k12.text: The Black Oath knights ride the far Crownlands and burn the outlying farms. My knights cannot leave the walls. You can. Ten of them, and the farmers can bring in the harvest.
k12.fin: Ten fewer oathbreakers. The farmers sent you a cheese. I ate it. You understand.

k13.title: The Siege Ogres
k13.text: The oathbreakers have hired ogres from the hills to break the outer farms' walls. If they bring those brutes to the moat, we will have a real siege. End them in the field.
k13.fin: No ogres at the moat. The King will sleep tonight, and so will I.

k14.title: Clear the Kingsroad
k14.text: The Marches will not be safe until the Red Hand learns that the road bites back. Take the fight to anything that moves out there.
k14.fin: The caravan masters have started calling that stretch of road by your name. Not all the names are polite.

varric.name: Commander Varric
varric.title: Commander of Lorenmar
varric.hello: Lorenmar still stands because people like you keep walking out of its gates. What do you need?

aldous.name: Father Aldous
aldous.title: Cathedral of Lorenmar
aldous.hello: The Light keeps you, child. Sit a while if you are weary.

thorin.name: Blacksmith Thorin
thorin.title: Smithy
thorin.hello: Mind the sparks. If it can be forged, I can forge it, given the right materials.

mara.name: Innkeeper Mara
mara.title: The Gilded Tankard
mara.hello: Warm food, cold ale and every rumour in Aldara. Pick one.

maren.name: Scout Maren
maren.title: Green Fields Outpost
maren.hello: Keep your voice down. The goblins have sharp ears.

dask.name: Ranger Dask
dask.title: Ashen Highlands Outpost
dask.hello: Ash in the wind, bones in the dirt. Welcome to the Highlands.

ilse.name: Warden Ilse
ilse.title: Shadowfen Outpost
ilse.hello: Stay on the boardwalks and stay alive. The bog takes the careless.

brom.name: Huntsman Brom
brom.title: Frostpeak Outpost
brom.hello: Cold enough to freeze your words in the air. Speak quickly.

kael.name: Ashwalker Kael
kael.title: Emberwaste Outpost
kael.hello: Breathe through the cloth. The ash will scour your lungs.

vhal.name: Seer Vhal
vhal.title: Void Reach Outpost
vhal.hello: I saw you coming three days ago. You were taller in the vision.

seraphine.name: Lady Seraphine
seraphine.title: Elysian Outpost
seraphine.hello: These lands were holy once. We will make them so again.

roderic.name: Captain Roderic Vale
roderic.title: Captain of the Sunset Gate
roderic.hello: Another traveller who made it through the Marches alive. You have my respect, and the Crown has work for someone like you.

topics.x: You stand in the royal capital of Aldara. Three walls, one moat, four great gates and more people than you have seen in your life. The Lower City is the Commons. Past the sandstone wall is the Middle Ward, where the three peoples keep their quarters. The white wall rings the Royal Ward and the palace. Keep to the avenues and you will not get lost.

Deserters, cutthroats and debtors who ran from the law. They wear a red handprint on their cloaks and they call their leader Red Jack, the King of Thieves. Ten years ago the Kingsroad was the safest road in the realm. Now caravans go out forty strong or not at all.

The Sunset Gate faces west, towards the Gloomwood and far-off Lorenmar. The Dawn Gate faces the sea. The Harvest Gate opens on the southern farms and the Crown Gate on the north road to the quarries. Each has a portcullis of dwarven steel that no ram has ever broken.

hale.name: Sergeant Hale
hale.title: City Watch, Lower City
hale.hello: Mind your purse and mind the grates. The Watch has enough trouble up here without anyone going missing down there.

topics.x: Under our feet runs the Undercity: aqueducts, cisterns and tunnels older than the walls. Some say the first kings found them already here, built by a people nobody remembers. The sewers flow through them now. So do the rats, and the rats down there are the size of dogs.

The sewermen whisper about a Rat King. A thing that wears a crown of bottle caps and bones, that the rats obey like soldiers. I thought it was a story to frighten apprentices. Then three of my watchmen went down after a thief and only one came back up.

elyndra.name: Loremaster Elyndra
elyndra.title: Keeper of the Moonwell
elyndra.hello: Be welcome in Silverbough, traveller. The Moonwell remembers every face that looks into it. Yours is new.

topics.x: We came east from the Elysian Expanse when the Seraphim fell and the holy groves turned against us. King Aldric the Unbowed gave us this quarter and asked nothing in return but our oath. We have kept it for nine hundred years, which to us is not so very long.

Its water was carried from the Elysian springs in the hands of our elders, drop by drop, over a year of walking. Under the full moon it glows silver. Drink from it and you will dream of the old forests. Drink too often and you will not want to wake.

The forest west of the Crownlands was the Queen's own garden once. Then the blight came, and the Hexwood Coven came with it: witches who bargain with things in the dark. The wyverns nest in the dead oaks now. My kin will not walk there.

durgan.name: Forgemaster Durgan Ironhand
durgan.title: Keeper of the Great Forge
durgan.hello: Hah! Mind the heat, longlegs. This fire was lit in the Deepforge before your grandfather's grandfather was a squalling babe.

topics.x: When the mountains shook and Ironhold under the stone was lost, we carried the first fire up in a lantern of star-iron. Our oath to the Crown is bound to that flame. If the Great Forge ever goes cold, the oath is ended and Ironhold goes home. So it will never go cold. Not while I live.
Ever wonder why the gates hold? Dwarven steel, folded nine hundred times and quenched in water from the Moonwell. The elves grumble about the water every year. They still send it.

chamberlain.name: Lord Chamberlain Aldous Wren
chamberlain.title: Keeper of the King's Door
chamberlain.hello: You wish to see His Majesty? Everyone wishes to see His Majesty. Fortunately for you, the King is fond of travellers with dust on their boots.

topics.x: Oswin the Fourth, called the Patient. He took the throne young, after his father fell to the Oathbreakers at Ashford, and he has spent thirty years mending what that betrayal broke. He listens more than he speaks. Those who mistake that for weakness do not do so twice.
Her Majesty is of Silverbough. When she wed the King, the Accord of Three Crowns was renewed in the Crown Plaza before the whole city. The elves wept. The dwarves pretended not to.

It is an old custom. Those who cross the Marches and come before the throne may kneel and receive the King's Blessing: a token of the Crown's favour. It will not make you a hero. It may help keep you alive long enough to become one.

caldwell.name: Lord Marshal Caldwell
caldwell.title: Marshal of the King's Guard
caldwell.hello: Stand straight. I have ten thousand soldiers and not one of them can leave the walls. That is where you come in.

topics.x: The Order of the Black Oath. Knights sworn to the old king who turned on him at the Battle of Ashford for the promise of land. They were cast out and cursed, and they have been raiding the Crownlands ever since, grey and silent in their black plate.

Blue cloaks on the walls, crimson on the Royal Knights. Elven wardens on the Silverbough lanes and dwarven ironguard in Ironhold. The Watch keeps the streets. My knights keep the King. Between us, nothing gets past the moat.

temperance.name: Archivist Temperance
temperance.title: Royal Library of Valcrest
temperance.hello: Quietly, please. Some of these books are older than the walls, and a few of them bite.

topics.x: Nine hundred and twelve years ago, Aldric the Unbowed broke the Iron Horde on this very hill. He planted his sword in the earth where the Crown Plaza fountain now stands and swore that a city would rise there that would never fall while three peoples held it together. It has not fallen.

Humans, the elves of Silverbough and the dwarves of Ironhold. Three peoples, three oaths, carved into the Accord Stone in the Crown Plaza. The humans swore to rule justly, the elves to heal and remember, the dwarves to build and defend. Read the stone yourself: the words still glow.

The granite Commons Wall was raised against the Iron Horde. The sandstone ring was built by the dwarves in return for Ironhold's quarter. The white wall of the Royal Ward was the elves' gift: they sang the marble out of the quarries, or so they claim.
Lorenmar was founded as the western bastion of the realm, the last walled town before the wilds. Commander Varric holds it in the King's name. It has had a hard century. Everything west of it has.

lysander.name: Lysander the Bard
lysander.title: Minstrel of the Crown Plaza
lysander.hello: A new face! Tell me a story and I will tell you three. Mine are better, but that is the price of admission.

topics.x: Sir Gareth the Steadfast, who held the Sunset Gate alone for a night and a day. Aelindra Swiftbow of Silverbough, whose arrow found the Horde-king's eye at four hundred paces. Thrain Anvilheart of Ironhold, who forged the first gate of the city with his own hands. Their statues stand in the Hall of Heroes. Mine will too, one day.

Every midsummer the lists by the barracks fill with knights from every corner of Aldara. The champion dines with the King. Last year it was an elven archer who had never held a lance. The knights are still sulking.

Aldric the Unbowed, who founded the city. Ysolde the Wise, who wrote the laws. Edric the Builder, who raised the Middle Ward. Oswin the Third, who fell at Ashford. Their statues line the Royal Avenue. Oswin the Fourth sits the throne now, and is in no hurry to become a statue.

solenne.name: High Priestess Solenne
solenne.title: Cathedral of the Dawn
solenne.hello: The Light keeps you, child. You have walked a long, dark road to reach this door.

topics.x: Before the Seraphim fell, the Light spoke through them. Now it speaks through small things: a candle that will not go out, a shrine someone still tends by the roadside. The Cathedral of the Dawn was built so that the Light would always have a house, even when its angels are gone.
You have been to the Elysian Expanse? Then you have seen what the Seraphim became. Some of us still pray for them. Some of us pray that they stay where they are.

hilda.name: Hilda Stonebarrel
hilda.title: Brewmistress of Ironhold
hilda.hello: You look like someone who needs a proper ale. Not that elven flower-water. A proper one.

topics.x: Our quarter sits on the north-east of the Middle Ward, close to the Great Forge where it belongs. We dug our cellars deeper than the Undercity. We did not like what we found down there, so we bricked it up again.

Word in the taverns is that the Red Hand pays someone inside the walls for news of the caravans. Word is also that Red Jack wears a stolen crown. Word is also that I water the ale. Only two of those are true.

tobias.name: Old Tobias
tobias.title: Beggar of the Commons
tobias.hello: Spare a thought, friend? Coins are nice, but I will take a thought.

topics.x: Most of the city lives out here in the Lower City: the millers, the carters, the washerwomen and the rest. The nobles look down on us from the Royal Ward. We look up at their gardens and grow cabbages.
I was at Ashford, you know. Carried the old king's banner. I saw the black knights turn their horses around. I saw him fall. They gave me a coin and a crutch for it. The crutch was better made.

king.name: King Oswin IV
king.title: King of Aldara
king.hello: So. You are the one who crossed the Marches. Come closer. I would see the face of someone the Red Hand could not stop.

topics.x: Aldara is wounded, not broken. The west burns with monsters, the Marches belong to thieves and the Gloomwood to witches. My father trusted the wrong knights at Ashford. I have spent my life trying to deserve the trust of better ones.
Maelis? She is wiser than I am and more patient, which is a hard thing to be in a family called the Patient. If you want to know what the elves really think of us, ask her. Be ready for the answer.
Varric writes to me every month. His letters are short and his requests are long. Tell him the Crown has not forgotten the west. Tell him I am sending what I can. It is never enough.

queen.name: Queen Maelis
queen.title: Queen of Aldara, of Silverbough
queen.hello: The Moonwell showed me your face three nights ago. You are exactly as tired as you looked.

topics.x: Three peoples, one city. It works because each of us believes the others would fall without them. Perhaps we are all right.
I was born under the Seraphim's light. I watched it turn cold. Some nights I still walk the Moonwell's edge and pretend the water is the old springs.

lore.x: Three oaths are carved into the black stone, and they still glow. In the common tongue: "We will rule justly." In the elven script, silver: "We will heal, and we will remember." In dwarven runes, fire-gold: "We will build, and we will defend." Beneath them, in Aldric's own hand: "While these three hold, the city stands."

King Aldric the Unbowed raises his sword over the city he founded. The plaque reads: "Here the Iron Horde broke. Here the sword was planted. Here the city rose." Children throw coins into the basin for luck. The Watch fishes them out on feast days and gives them to the poor.

Four statues ring the square before the Hall of Heroes. The plaques name the defenders of the city in every age, from Sir Gareth the Steadfast to the knights who held the moat during the last Horde raid. There is an empty plinth at the end of the row. Nobody will say who it is for.

The water glows faintly silver even by day. A carved ring of elven verse runs around the rim: "Carried from the springs of the Seraphim, drop by drop, a year of walking. Remember the groves." A few coins glint at the bottom. They are not coins. They are silver leaves.

The heat reaches you from across the square. A bronze plaque, too hot to touch: "This fire was carried up from the Deepforge of Ironhold in a lantern of star-iron. While it burns, the oath of Ironhold is kept." Below it someone has scratched: "and while it burns, the ale is warm".

A black obelisk carved with the names of every Royal Archivist since the founding. The newest name is Temperance. The oldest has been worn away by nine centuries of scholars touching it for luck before their examinations.
A painted board lists the champions of the Midsummer Tourney. The last name, freshly painted, is an elf of Silverbough. Someone has added a small drawing of a knight crying into his helmet.

The westernmost gate, facing the Gloomwood road and, far beyond it, Lorenmar. Its arch bears the scars of the Iron Horde's rams, left unrepaired on purpose. An inscription: "They broke upon these stones. So will the next."
The eastern gate faces the sea. On the longest day of the year the sunrise shines straight down the Royal Avenue through the Dawn Gate and lights the Founder's sword in the Crown Plaza.

Carts from the southern farms pour through here every morning. Carved grain sheaves frame the arch, and a tally board counts the harvest wagons since midsummer. This year's count is low. The Oathbreakers have been burning the fields.

The northern gate on the road to the quarries, where the white marble of the Royal Ward was cut. Its portcullis is dwarven steel. A notice: "By order of the Marshal, the Crown Gate closes at dusk. Oathbreakers ride the northern roads."
The doors are bronze, cast with the story of the Seraphim: their coming, their shining age and their fall. The last panel is blank. The priests say it is waiting for the Seraphim to rise again.

The palace has stood since Edric the Builder raised it three hundred years after the founding. The great doors are open by day. The Royal Knights at the stair will let you pass if you mean the King no harm, and they are very good at telling.
The tallest elven tower in the city. A crystal at its peak catches moonlight and holds it all night, so that Silverbough is never truly dark. The elves say it was grown, not built.
A great brass telescope turns slowly under the dome. A chalk board by the door lists the stars that have gone out in the last hundred years. The list is longer than it should be.

cry: Hear ye! The King holds court in the palace today!
Fresh bread from the Commons ovens!
The Red Hand has been seen on the Kingsroad. Travel armed!
By order of the Watch: stay out of the Undercity!
Silverbough honey wine, straight from the Moonwell groves!
Ironhold steel, the finest in Aldara!
Midsummer Tourney entries are open at the lists!
The Great Forge has not gone cold in nine hundred years!
